_schema: One station, in the shape M3 fixed and M4 and M5 added to. M6 adds one field and it is a station's business rather than a canvas's: `when` on a canvas, the ISO date behind the words the holder prints, so that tools/station.py can ask whether a canvas is inside its station's span and say so when it is not.
title: The wheatfield
_canvases: One canvas, and the piece does not need a second. DESIGN 7 asks for three paths, crows, and the rush with no holds, and then for the strokes to stop arriving. Two of those three are in the canvas. The crows are not built -- DESIGN 7 wants them in the corner of the eye since Arles and M6 does not have them, which is named in BUILD rather than faked here.

canvases.title: Wheatfield with Crows
canvases.note: 103 by 50.5 cm: a double square, and the widest thing in the piece. DESIGN 9 says the frame of the world widens here and that the viewer will feel it and not notice; what actually widens is the canvas, which is a fact about 1890 and not an effect. At the fixed 50 degrees every canvas is hung at, this one covers the same width of the world as the Harvest and half the height, so the paint arrives as a band. BUILD.md M6 records what a fixed painting distance would do instead and why that decision is not M6's to take.

_ground: The plain under it, on the same terms as station 4: a plane the horizon puts at eye level, with a swell along the ray. Flatter than La Crau because this is not the Crau -- the fields above Auvers roll and the canvas says so.
_volume: M6 sets this. DESIGN 15's volume question was open from M3 to M6 with three possible answers written down, and the one that turned out to be true is the third: the instrument was wrong. `nearEdge` counts time spent within half a metre of the boundary, which any walker with a net forward drift accumulates simply by arriving there -- forty seconds at 1.45 m/s is 58 metres, so M3's sweep answering '50 by 40' was measuring the walk and not the volume. `pressing` counts time spent holding a key that would go further out while the ground takes the body back: trying to leave rather than standing at the edge. Swept at station 4 with the `look` walker, which is the only one of the three that stops and turns and looks: 27.0% at 12 by 7, 20.6% at 18 by 11, **12.7% at 26 by 16** and 0.0% at 40 by 25. So this is the first size in the sweep that comes under the fifth M3 pre-registered, and it is two to three times the old slab rather than the seven M3 feared. What it costs is a thin far field: the plain is a quarter of its own density by six metres out and this walks to twenty-six. `wander` still fails here at 49.6% and always will, because an amble in a straight line for forty seconds is not something any bounded place absorbs.
_weave: Auvers cloth, ordinary primed linen again after the jute of Saint-Remy.
_pacing: The rush with no holds. burst is twice every other station's and hold is zero, and both are the design's words made into numbers rather than a measurement -- M2's constant says how fast the record thinks he painted and this says how fast the piece plays it back. It is the only station that overrides the burst, and BUILD.md M6 says what it costs. M8: and it is the last thing that plays itself. Autoplay stops at this canvas's last stroke, because past it there is nothing left to paint; the road out of the back of the field, and station 11 at the end of it, are reached with a hand on the scrub or not at all.
_crows: Three in the air, to either side of the canvas and behind. The crows in it are paint and stay where he put them; these have been at the edge of the frame since Arles.
_letter: The edition's note on this sentence names the two likeliest canvases, and this is one of them: Wheatfield under Troubled Skies (F 778) at station 9 and Wheatfield with Crows (F 779) here, both at the Van Gogh Museum. The line stops before the rest of the sentence, which says what he was trying to express: DESIGN 9 asks for the working painter and not the biography, and what the ending means is M8's to get right. M3 cited 902, his last letter to Theo, which names no canvas here. M8 keeps it. It is about the work -- the canvases he was making that week and what they were of -- which is what DESIGN 9 asks a line to be, and it arrives after the rush has ended, in the silence over the finished field, as the last words in the piece. The half of the sentence it stops before is about what he meant the canvases to express, and it stays out for the reason station 7 has no letter at all: the shape of the piece says that, and his words here are the working painter's.

letter.to: Theo van Gogh and Jo van Gogh-Bonger
letter.text: They’re immense stretches of wheatfields under turbulent skies…

_caption: M8 takes the commentary out of this caption and leaves the plaque, and does the same at station 7. Everywhere else the caption carries what is measured and what is not, because that is worth re-reading; at the two beats it would be the piece explaining itself at the one moment it must not. What it said is still true and is here: the canvas is a double square, twice as wide as it is tall, and it is the last station with paint in it; its strokes arrive at twice the rate of anywhere else and nothing punctuates them, which is the one number at this station that is a decision rather than a measurement.
